title: The keystone ten meet the clinic: is estimator dominance clinically marked or clinically silent?
question: [ecology] Do the ten cases that carry 79.29% of the idea-046 band-2/3 reversal differ in aggregate on released 3-month mRS, admission NIHSS, and demographics from the other 89 -- and is their dominance proportionate to deficit burden, or keystone-like (disproportionate per unit burden)?
register: descriptive-association. Operator steering note of 2026-09-02 (evidence/decisions.md) requests exactly this successor in the descriptive register and explicitly excludes model-use formulations of this direction; the wide-track deliverable template ('the model is using X') is overridden for this candidate by that human-authored direction.
lineage_note: Enters as a separately registered successor citing the idea-046 census and debate, per ideas/046/interpretation.md Next-decision item 4. The phenotype join was pre-registered 2026-08-28 and never executed.
design_template_justification: The lineage direction is definitionally observational (aggregate description of frozen strata). Diversity across this cycle's set is carried by c02 (natural-paired) and c03 (other:value-lattice-audit); no two candidates share a grammar.
borrowed_construct: Ecology's keystone-species / community-importance index (Power et al. 1996, BioScience 46:609-620, DOI 10.2307/1312990): a keystone's impact is disproportionate to its abundance. Implied measurement: contribution per unit 'abundance' -- regress |c_i| on label-blind deficit burden and separate burden-proportionate dominance (expected, arithmetic) from disproportionate dominance (the keystone reading).
deliverable_sentence: In the frozen 99-case idea-046 census cohort, the high-contribution stratum does / does not differ in aggregate on a pre-frozen released clinical variable list (3-month mRS, admission NIHSS, age, sex, plus treatment fields if present in the release) from the remaining cases, and its dominance is / is not accounted for by deficit burden -- an exploratory, aggregate-only, association-register description under the D3 read-restriction and D4 joint-display rules, with no per-patient claims and no model probing.
X_measurement: Per-case signed contribution c_i and rank, already frozen in probes/046/results/results_v3/per_case_contributions.csv (columns case_id, d_band2, d_band3, delta, contribution, signed_rank). Label-blind deficit burden: eroded Tmax>6s deficit-region voxel count per case, recomputable from the held maps with the ratified take-13 region machinery (no outcome contact). Disproportionality: residual of |c_i| on burden. Clinical variables: ses-02 outcome.csv and ses-01 demographic_baseline.csv per case, with the variable list frozen from the record-level clinical_data-description.xlsx (12.1 kB, on the Zenodo record) BEFORE any case-level file is read.
use_vs_association: No use claim is made anywhere: the candidate is deliberately in the association register per the operator steering note. The discriminating content of the design is between two descriptive readings -- burden-proportionate dominance versus disproportionate (keystone) dominance -- not between use and association.
keystone_prerequisite: (1) The frozen per-case contribution table exists in-repo under the ratified census; (2) per-case phenotype files carrying the ses-02 outcome family and ses-01 baseline variables exist inside the held, checksum-verified training archive.
keystone_evidence: (1) probes/046/results/results_v3/per_case_contributions.csv on main: header 'case_id,d_band2,d_band3,delta,contribution,signed_rank', 99 data rows, top row 'sub-stroke0153,...,0.007141719141395045,1'; top-10 signed head share 0.7928912778985707 in census_summary.json (top_k 10); 39 negative contributions (census_summary.json 'negative': 39). (2) Archive payload, from git origin/results/probe-023-349af5ad0b3e:probes/023/results_v2/archive_manifest.csv (manifest of the md5-verified train.7z): rows 'train/phenotype/sub-stroke0001/ses-01/sub-stroke0001_ses-01_demographic_baseline.csv,405,184c4588' and 'train/phenotype/sub-stroke0001/ses-02/sub-stroke0001_ses-02_outcome.csv,98,6f8fa8cd'; grep counts 149 ses-02_outcome.csv members and 149 demographic_baseline.csv members.
verified_dataset_facts: Zenodo record 16813698 (v3, 2025-08-12): open access, license 'Creative Commons Attribution Non Commercial Share Alike 4.0 International'; files train.7z (99.0 GB) and clinical_data-description.xlsx (12.1 kB); description states clinical data 'demographics, patient history, admission NIHSS, 3-month functional outcome (mRS), etc.' and '149 acute ischemic stroke cases'. This is the exact record this program holds (md5 36ae28b9... match recorded in evidence/decisions.md, 2026-08-25).
Dataset paper arXiv:2408.11142 (Radiology: AI DOI 10.1148/ryai.250603): follow-up MRI at 2-9 days; 'delineated infarction masks in follow-up MRI'; multicenter, 245 cases total across splits.

Challenge paper arXiv:2408.10966: training n=150 with hidden test set (abstract fetch reported 150/98; a secondary read of the updated version reported 149/96); the held training payload contains 149 cases -- payload count outranks prose per the 2026-08-25 standing lesson.
The 99 analyzed census cases are the take-13 cohort (149 minus exclusions; sub-stroke0043 source-defective member excluded per contract policy).
smallest_decisive_experiment: Freeze the analysis spec in the card/contract before any case-level phenotype read: (a) variable list taken from clinical_data-description.xlsx only; (b) two frozen contrasts -- census top-10 versus rest (stratum already frozen by the ratified census) and disproportionality top-decile versus rest; (c) statistics limited to standardized mean differences and rank tests with permutation nulls at n=99, all variables reported (no selective reporting); (d) every clinical contrast displayed jointly with deficit burden per D4; (e) phenotype staging and reads restricted to the 99 analyzed identifiers per D3. Then stage the ~50 kB of phenotype CSVs for the 99 ids, compute, and report one aggregate table. CPU-only, minutes.
compute_envelope: Trivial: CPU-only, under five minutes of compute; data staged is two 99-file CSV families totaling ~50 kB plus one 12.1 kB description file. No GPU. Fits any Colab session with margin.
most_dangerous_confound: Deficit-burden mediation (the program's own critique D4): larger deficits both dominate the estimator arithmetic and predict worse clinical outcomes for ordinary reasons, so 'keystones are sicker' can be pure volume. Addressed by construction: the disproportionality axis separates per-unit-burden dominance from size, and D4 joint display plus aggregate-only claims prevent a mediated association being read as a clinical subtype finding.
standing_confounds_addressed: (1) D4 volume mediation -- see most_dangerous_confound. (2) Opened outcomes: the 99 imaging outcomes were read in idea-023, so the candidate is exploratory by construction and says so; freezing definitions before computation is a discipline commitment, not blindness (ideas/046/feasibility.md). (3) Multiplicity: frozen short variable list, permutation nulls, all-variables reporting. (4) Selection: both strata are frozen by prior ratified artifacts before any clinical value is seen. (5) Clinical scores remain unread until the frozen spec exists; the D3 protocol governs the staging.
dies_like_prior: IDENTIFIABILITY_FAILURE (x12) killed model-use attributions; this candidate makes no use claim and its main rival reading (volume mediation) is built into the design as a measured axis rather than left as a confound. DATA_ACCESS (x3): all inputs verified present -- frozen census table in-repo, phenotype files in the held checksum-verified archive. EFFECT_UNREACHABLE (x1): not applicable; no effect-size floor is claimed.
closest_prior_work: Broocks et al., Radiology 2024 (DOI 10.1148/radiol.231750, PMID 39078297): in 721 private-cohort patients, showed rCBF-threshold core overestimation is clinically marked (larger baseline core, successful recanalization). Exact delta: they profile deviation from a single fixed threshold on a private cohort; this candidate profiles frozen per-case contribution shares of a band contrast on a public benchmark, adds the per-unit-burden keystone axis, and is bound to pre-registered read-restriction and joint-display rules.
novelty_neighbors: Maier-Hein et al., 'Why rankings of biomedical image analysis competitions should be interpreted with care', Nature Communications 2018, DOI 10.1038/s41467-018-07619-7 -- benchmark conclusions hinge on test-set composition (bootstrap over cases), but no frozen per-case contribution census and no clinical profiling of influential cases.

de la Rosa et al., 'ISLES'24: Final Infarct Prediction with Multimodal Imaging and Clinical Data', arXiv:2408.10966 -- the organizers use the clinical variables as model inputs for prediction; no influence decomposition, no dominant-versus-rest description.
Broocks et al., Radiology 2024, DOI 10.1148/radiol.231750 -- closest in spirit; delta as stated in closest_prior_work.
novelty_delta: No published secondary analysis joining ISLES'24 imaging with its released phenotype tables was found by search (one unconfirmed near-miss: Tomography 2026, DOI 10.3390/tomography12030029, full text inaccessible); the specific object -- descriptive clinical profiling of a frozen estimator-dominance census with a burden-normalized keystone axis -- appears unpublished.
why_not_done: NEW_CAPABILITY: the frozen, ratified per-case contribution census (probes/046/results/results_v3, imported 2026-09-01) exists only inside this program, and the ISLES'24 phenotype tables have been public only since 2024-2025.
audience_relevance: Anyone reusing threshold- or band-based perfusion contrasts on this public benchmark inherits the head-dominance the census proved; whether the dominant cases are clinically marked or clinically silent determines whether such contrasts can be read as clinical-subgroup phenomena or must be read as imaging-geometry artifacts -- either answer disciplines a common analysis pattern on a widely used dataset.
unverified_claims: Exact column names and coding of outcome.csv and demographic_baseline.csv (mitigation: the record-level clinical_data-description.xlsx is read and the variable list frozen before any case-level file).
Presence of treatment/reperfusion fields in the released tables (the Zenodo description says 'etc.'; the card treats treatment variables as conditional-if-present).
Per-case deficit-burden extraction reuses take-13 region machinery label-blind; confirmed at spec time, not yet re-run.
The Tomography 2026 near-miss (DOI 10.3390/tomography12030029) could not be read in full; whether it joins ISLES'24 phenotype tables is unconfirmed.

clarity.why: Two precise frozen contrasts on a frozen cohort with a frozen variable list; slightly below 5 because the treatment-variable arm is conditional on release contents.

identifiability.why: For a descriptive claim, the design rules out the main alternative reading (volume mediation) via the disproportionality axis and D4 joint display; residual ambiguity from small strata and observational structure is irreducible and stated.

medical_relevance.why: Determines whether a reproducible perfusion-band phenomenon on a public benchmark tracks clinical severity; plausible utility for how such contrasts are interpreted, no direct care consequence.

interest.why: Program-central and operator-requested; outside the program it is a useful niche result about who carries benchmark-scale contrasts.

prior_legwork.why: Census frozen and ratified in-repo; phenotype in the held archive; D3/D4 protocols already written and ratified; take-13 region machinery complete.

feasibility.why: Minutes of CPU on ~50 kB of staged data; every input verified; keystone INSPECTED_TRUE lifts the cap.

data_readiness.why: Archive held and checksum-verified; phenotype requires one small D3-restricted staging event rather than being already extracted.

evaluation_readiness.why: No accepted metric for 'clinically marked'; custom descriptive comparisons with permutation nulls must be pre-frozen.

negative_result_value.why: A null (clinically silent keystones) is sensitivity-limited at 10-versus-89 but still interpretable and useful: it pushes the reversal's explanation toward imaging geometry and warns against clinical readings of band contrasts.

novelty_confidence.why: Searched: no ISLES'24 phenotype-join secondary analysis found; nearest work (Broocks 2024) differs in cohort, estimand, and design; the census object is unique to this program. Not 5: absence of evidence from search is not proof.

regret.why: Pre-registered 2026-08-28, never executed, and explicitly requested by the operator steering note; skipping it again would be obvious-in-hindsight.

plain_pitch: An earlier experiment in this program found that a puzzling reversal in how stroke lesions relate to blood-flow levels is carried almost entirely by about ten of 99 patients. Nobody yet knows who those ten patients are in clinical terms. This idea takes the dataset's released clinical records -- for example, how disabled each patient was three months after the stroke -- and asks, in aggregate only, whether the dominant patients look clinically different from the rest, or whether they stand out only for imaging-arithmetic reasons such as having large affected regions. Either answer changes how researchers should read blood-flow-threshold comparisons on this public dataset; because these patients' images were already examined earlier, the idea is exploratory by construction and makes no claim about any individual patient.
